title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts
body: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, while a third pumps it to the rest of the body. When an octopus swims, the main heart stops beating — which is why they prefer crawling. Swimming exhausts them!

title: Honey Never Spoils
body: Archaeologists have found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still perfectly edible. Honey's low moisture content and acidic pH create an environment where bacteria simply cannot survive.

title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year
body: Venus takes 243 Earth days to rotate once on its axis, but only 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun. So a single day on Venus is about 18% longer than its entire year!

title: Bananas Are Berries, Strawberries Aren't
body: Botanically speaking, a berry must develop from a single ovary flower. Bananas qualify, but strawberries don't — their seeds are on the outside because they come from multiple ovaries.

title: The Impossible Knot
body: Mathematicians proved in 2017 that any knot made with a string can be untangled — but the number of steps can grow exponentially. A knot with 10 crossings might need over a billion steps to untie!

title: Clouds Weigh Millions of Pounds
body: A typical cumulus cloud contains about 500 tons of water droplets. That's roughly 1.1 million pounds floating 20,000 feet in the sky. They don't fall because the water is distributed across billions of tiny droplets.

title: The Smallest Magic Trick Ever
body: The quantum Zeno effect is nature's own magic trick: a quantum system can be frozen in time simply by observing it frequently enough. Scientists call it 'a watched pot never boils' — but it's literally true!

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Energy
body: Despite being only 2% of your body weight, your brain consumes about 20% of your total energy. It generates enough electricity to power a small light bulb, and processes information at speeds up to 268 mph.

title: The Library of Babel
body: A library containing every possible 410-page book would have more books than atoms in the observable universe. Almost every book would be nonsense — but in there somewhere is your complete life story.

title: Shadows Can Collide
body: When two shadows overlap, the combined shadow can be darker than either alone. This is because shadows aren't objects — they're the absence of light. Where two light-blockers meet, even less light reaches the surface.
